clue.text: A vacuous bassist holding note in Help!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the emptied word clasps the note between its two letters
a vacuous word is emptied of its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: Someone asks for assistance from a rather empty-headed bass player.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: I'm very annoyed composer drops third key

indicators.note: the composer's name lets go of a letter, which is removed from it

parts.note: J. S. Bach the composer
the third letter of the composer's name is C, which is also a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a composer has left out a key from his work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third key' does double duty in the surface but names one thing: the third letter of BACH, a C, which is also a key in music.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of irritation or contempt expresses strong annoyance.

clue.text: Son in country heads south for an experience

indicators.note: in a down answer, going south means moving lower; the son at the head of the word moves down

parts.note: a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A son living abroad sets off southwards in search of a new experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that begins STATE is the son 'in country'; 'heads south' moves it down two places to give TASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To taste something is to have a brief experience of it, as in tasting freedom.

clue.text: Bloomer in allegory must be corrected

indicators.note: something needing correction is wrong as it stands, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A mistake in an allegorical tale has to be put right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' wants to mean a blunder, which suits the surface's correction; here it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A flower is something that blooms, and this lily is a flower with orange petals.

clue.text: Disgusting old boy spotted getting picked up

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: picked up as by the ear: a word heard rather than read

parts.note: spotted means seen

explanation.surface: A former pupil was seen doing something revolting and was arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests an arrest, but it signals that SEEN is heard, and spelt SCENE.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene material is offensive and repugnant, causing revulsion.

clue.text: Seasonal work one might get in a book store?

definitions.text: Seasonal work one might get in a book store?

parts.words: Seasonal work one might get in a book store
parts.note: read as a holiday job at a bookshop, but it means a festive literary work stocked by one, the Dickens novella

explanation.surface: A temporary Christmas job serving customers at a bookshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1843 novella about Christmas is a seasonal literary work sold in bookshops.

clue.text: Knight a convict turned over and conned

indicators.note: turned over means the letters read in reverse order in this down light

parts.note: taken as written
a lag is British slang for a convict, especially an old lag
to be had is to be tricked, so had means conned

explanation.surface: A knight was robbed by a convict and swindled.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Men with law row about something used in south London courts

definitions.text: something used in south London courts

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lawyers quarrel over something in the law courts of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courts' suggests law courts, as do 'law' and 'row'; the courts are the grass tennis courts at Wimbledon in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine for cutting grass is used to keep the grass tennis courts at Wimbledon trim.

clue.text: Foreigners hail units struggling to detain a knight

indicators.note: to detain is to hold inside, so the anagram keeps the other letters within it
struggling suggests the letters are in disorder and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Foreign visitors greet military units battling to hold a knight captive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hail' tempts as a greeting and 'units' as soldiers; both are only letters for the anagram, which then holds the two inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: People from Lithuania are foreigners to anyone outside that Baltic country.

clue.text: Good entertainer primarily shines and glimmers

parts.note: a host entertains guests

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the opening letter of shines

explanation.surface: A good performer stands out, glittering on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint trace or hint of something, like the ghost of a smile, is a glimmer.

clue.text: Ticket comedian gets son to see The Blockheads

parts.note: a half is a child's ticket at half fare in Britain
a wit is a clever, funny person

explanation.surface: A comic and his son buy tickets for a gig by the band The Blockheads.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blockheads were Ian Dury's band, which the capital letters exploit; here they are simply blockheads, idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Blockheads are stupid people, dimwits lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Super with force receives old, then current, order

indicators.note: receives means takes in, so one piece is placed inside the others

parts.note: ace means excellent, super
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A superior officer with the police takes an old command, then a current one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' simply puts the current, I, after everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acoemeti were an ancient monastic order of 'sleepless' monks who kept up continuous prayer.

clue.text: Obedient class welcomed by Tory expert

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by, so the class goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
able means skilled, expert
a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A compliant class is greeted warmly by a Conservative specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformable means disposed to comply or submit, hence obedient.

clue.text: Sweet smell associated with Obsession?

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bug is a craze or obsession, as in the travel bug

explanation.surface: A fragrance with the brand name Obsession smells sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obsession' with its capital looks like the perfume; it means a bug, a craze. A humbug is a British boiled mint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a hard striped peppermint sweet sold in Britain.

clue.text: I get sudden spasms, not being properly assessed

indicators.note: spasms are convulsions, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient complains of sudden convulsions that doctors have failed to examine properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Information left unabsorbed has not been thought through or considered properly.

clue.text: One racing around in state due to lack of dope

indicators.note: around and in a state both suggest letters milling in disorder, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone running in a race is in a bad way because no drugs are available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' tempts as a drug, which suits racing; here it is information, as in getting the dope on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking information or knowledge is a state of not knowing, and dope is slang for information.

clue.text: Desire for topless flapper's ultimately prurient

indicators.note: topless means losing the top, the first letter

parts.note: a swan is a big bird that flaps its wings, a flapper

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of prurient

explanation.surface: A lustful longing for a topless 1920s flapper girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapper' suggests a 1920s party girl, and 'topless' and 'prurient' push that way; it is a swan, which flaps its wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and desire are synonyms for a longing or wish for something.

clue.text: German private providing cover for one leaving pit?

parts.note: own means personal, private

explanation.surface: A German soldier is shielding a miner coming up from the coal pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pit' suggests a coal mine and 'private' a soldier; pit is slang for bed, and a dressing gown covers someone getting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing gown is a robe worn over nightclothes by someone who has just got out of bed.

clue.text: New reparation for an old Italian leader

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are re-formed into another word

explanation.surface: Fresh compensation is paid to a former leader of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Praetorian Guard was the bodyguard serving the Roman emperors, ancient rulers in Italy.

clue.text: Informal President that's wrapping Zulu a gift

indicators.note: wrapping means enclosing, so the outer pieces surround the inner letter

parts.note: prez is informal shorthand for president
IE stands for id est, that is
Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A casual head of state is wrapping a present for a Zulu.
explanation.definitionFit: A prezzie is British informal slang for a present.

clue.text: Can year turn around uni kid who uses a crutch

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: turn around means the word for the university is read backwards

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is a university

explanation.surface: Can a year at university turn round a young student on crutches?
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Christmas story, Bob Cratchit's sickly young son walks with a crutch.

clue.text: Surface in sea abroad during, say, dive ultimately

indicators.note: during means inside the time of, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means here
mer is French for sea

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of dive

explanation.surface: A diver comes up to the surface of a foreign sea after a long dive.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come up out of water, to surface.

clue.text: Give particular direction to criminal in Alsace

indicators.note: criminal means wrong, lawless, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police steer a crook in the French region of Alsace.
explanation.definitionFit: To canalise something is to channel it, guiding it in a specific direction.

clue.text: Bloodsucker and one who acted as one seen by church

parts.note: Christopher Lee, the actor famous for playing Dracula, a bloodsucker

explanation.surface: A vampire and the actor who played one are spotted near a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' in 'acted as one' points back to the bloodsucker: Christopher Lee often played the vampire Dracula.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, also a parasitic person.

clue.text: One near English peak always catches bit of sleep

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain peak, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: catches means holds inside, so the sleep letter goes into always

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, always
Z, as in the zzz of a cartoon sleeper

explanation.surface: Someone living close to an English peak always manages a little sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near' means mean or stingy here: Ebenezer Scrooge is the miser of Dickens's tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old word for miserly, and Scrooge, Dickens's miser, has this first name.

clue.text: Start sweet after taking last two slices inside

indicators.text: after taking last two slices inside
indicators.note: the final pair of letters is cut off and slipped inside the rest of the word

parts.note: a toffee is a chewy sweet

explanation.surface: Begin on a dessert once the last two pieces have been taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of TOFFEE, EE, move inside it after the T to make TEEOFF; tee off is the opening shot in golf.
explanation.definitionFit: To tee off is to begin, literally to play the first shot of a hole in golf.

clue.text: Note having nothing on is cooler

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: having nothing means lacking an O, the round figure nought, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A musical note played naked is rather cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' loses its O (nothing) to leave N, which follows FA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is a device for cooling, by waving or by blowing air.

clue.text: Bruce Lee chewed, eating large middle bit of loaf

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the anagram swallows another letter
chewed means mangled, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: M is medium, the middle clothing size

explanation.surface: The martial-arts star Bruce Lee chewed while eating a big piece of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chewed' rearranges BRUCE LEE to CEREBEUL, which 'eating' fills with L; M (medium, the middle size) follows. 'loaf' is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaf is British slang for the head, and this is a part of the brain at its back.

clue.text: One might help find theme in second sections of Charles Dickens books!

indicators.note: the second section of each name is its second letter

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A clue to the puzzle's theme lies in the second parts of Dickens's books.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Dickens's A Christmas Carol. Take the second letters of Charles and Dickens, then NT for the books of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue or suggestion helps a solver find something, such as a puzzle's theme.
